title: SSH Works, but the Site Doesn't
symptom: The launch checklist says web-1 is ready: 'SSH in from the office works, nginx is running and listening on 443'. But customers can't load the site at all. The launch is in an hour.

goals.description: Customers can reach the site on web-1 over HTTPS

evidence.description: the site timing out from outside
which ports web-1's firewall actually lets in

question.prompt: Why can you SSH in but customers can't load the site?
options: The route table is missing the internet gateway route
web-sg only allows port 22 from the office range. There's no inbound rule for 443, so HTTPS is silently dropped while SSH (allowed) works

debrief: SSH working proved a lot: the instance is up, it has a public IP, the route to the internet gateway exists, and the NACL passes traffic. That narrows the problem to something port-specific, and the security group is the port-specific layer. web-sg allowed 22 from the office range and nothing else. Security groups deny by default and drop silently, so HTTPS timed out instead of being refused. The fix was one rule: 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. The trap was a different rule. Under launch pressure it's tempting to 'just open everything' or to open 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 while you're at it; that would have cost points here, and in real life exposed SSH gets brute-forced within minutes. Keep SSH restricted to the office range, or better, use SSM Session Manager and open no SSH port at all.
